title: Ir, Seguir and Venir + Gerund: Change Over Time

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *ir* + gerund, *venir* + gerund and *seguir* + gerund from B2 Unit 24 (*seguir* + gerund from A2 Unit 28 too). They show a process that moves forward step by step (*ir*), has built up until now (*venir*) or has not stopped (*seguir*). The story of immigration is exactly that: a neighbourhood slowly filling up.

sections.title: Gradual change and continuity
rows: El barrio se iba llenando de inmigrantes.
*ir* + gerund: it was gradually filling up
Los barcos iban llegando al puerto.
*ir* + gerund: the ships kept arriving, one after another
Muchos inmigrantes seguían hablando su lengua en casa.
*seguir* + gerund: they still spoke it, it had not stopped
El italiano y el español se iban mezclando en la calle.

items.spanish: El barrio se iba llenando de familias que venían de Italia y de España.
items.english: The neighbourhood was gradually filling up with families from Italy and Spain.

items.spanish: Los barcos iban llegando al puerto cada semana.
items.english: Ships kept arriving at the port every week.

items.spanish: Muchos inmigrantes seguían hablando su lengua en casa.
items.english: Many immigrants still spoke their language at home.

items.spanish: El italiano y el español se iban mezclando en la calle.
items.english: Italian and Spanish were gradually mixing in the street.

sections.content: *Iba llegando* is not a plan: *ir* + gerund (no *a*) shows a process, one step at a time. A note for later: people in Buenos Aires say *vos* where you learned *tú*; you will meet that form later in the course, so here you only need to know it exists.
